title: A session waiting on CI never sleeps through the result
why: Your gripe, Oct 26 ("how come I haven't seen much done in the past hours?"): nothing moved for about 2.5 hours. Batch #649's gates-macos job went red at 22:05 and green at 22:09; a run with a failed job sends no all-done event, a green job wakes nobody, and the build advisor had set no check-in, so it never woke.
note: Built on PR 651 (draft, in review). (1) Primary wake, owner's idea Oct 26: gates.yml's last job ci-done posts one PR comment when a run ends with a failed or cancelled job; a comment wakes the watching session. Shared action actions/ci-done-comment, so other repos can call it. Unmeasured: that a github-actions bot comment wakes a session; the first red batch run measures it. (2) Fallback rule git-ci-wait-checks-in: a session waiting on CI sets a send_later check-in on each wait and after each red job, wider each time; also in the ci-hygiene skill. (3) Stall check for standing roles in the project-ops operating model. (4) Platform ask for shiv: plans/c88-platform-ask.md in project files. The waiter guard rule refuses sleep loops in Bash only; send_later is a tool call, so it is not refused. Port: yes; the rule is global and the comment action is opt-in for each repo. Placed ahead of c82, after c53 (triage, Oct 26): an idle pipeline stops every lane at once. Measured Oct 27: a red batch run's ci-done comment on PR #663 woke the watching build advisor about 3 minutes after the check_run event (queued 02:13 UTC, arrived 02:15 UTC).
